primitives.name: Variance-Corrected Elo Update
primitives.verbatim_quote: b(θ_i - θ_j) + 1⁄2 b''(θ_i - θ_j)(σ_i2 + σ_j2) =: b(θ_i-θ_j) + K(θ_i-θ_j, σ_i, σ_j), where K is odd in its first argument and even in the other two.

The core innovation lies in modifying the standard Elo update rule to include a variance-dependent correction term K(θ_i - θ_j, σ_i, σ_j) = ½ b''(θ_i - θ_j)(σ_i² + σ_j²). This adjustment reflects that greater performance uncertainty should lead to smaller rating shifts. The derivation uses a Boltzmann-type equation and leads to a Fokker–Planck limit, showing convergence under certain conditions. The key insight is that the variance-corrected update stabilizes ratings by shrinking them toward team means when uncertainty increases. In GSE, this translates into a dynamic rating system that adapts to lineup changes and injury impacts. In GSI, it enables Bayesian uncertainty quantification through σ-dependent shrinkage. The convergence theorem ensures that ratings will asymptotically approach true strengths under idealized conditions, though real-world applications must account for finite team counts and structured schedules.
